headline: Multi-omics and machine learning nominate candidate genes across diverse diseases
label: Integrative Multi Omics Target Discovery
summary: Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic and network analyses are narrowing large datasets to short lists of candidate therapeutic and biomarker targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a move from multi-layer omics and bioinformatic datasets to short lists of candidate genes, typically combining transcriptomic or proteomic data with network analysis or machine learning feature selection. Ferroptosis recurs as an organizing theme across several items, including endometriosis, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (ALOX5), periodontitis and IBD (COPZ1), rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and serous ovarian cancer (KLF2). Phosphoproteomic mining extends the frame beyond transcription, as in RELL1 and the paralog-specific ROCK1 and ROCK2 networks mapped across thousands of datasets. Experimental validation varies: baicalein is tested in mesangial-cell rescue, KLF2 includes clinical validation, and the PFOA study pairs computational modeling with in vitro work. Novel elements include ALOX5 as a ferroptosis-associated driver of epithelial barrier dysfunction and a comparison of 113 machine learning model combinations for PFOA-associated MASLD.
